sections.label: Bill aims to attract listings
sections.summary: The Bill aims to attract more quality listings by supporting the new Global Listing Board with Nasdaq.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: This Bill aims to attract more quality listings in Singapore by enabling issuers to tap local and overseas capital conveniently.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: It will support the new Global Listing Board (GLB), an innovative listing bridge with Nasdaq, which was announced by the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) and SGX in November last year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: The GLB provides issuers a direct pathway to access capital across both markets with one prospectus and a harmonised set of rules.

sections.label: Equities market support initiatives
sections.summary: Initiatives include the Equity Market Development Programme allocating up to $6.5 billion, and trading volumes rose 32% in Q1 2026.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: Other initiatives announced by the Equities Market Review Group last year to support the demand and supply of capital include the Equity Market Development Programme, which will allocate up to $6.5 billion directly and also to crowd in private capital to deepen local fund management capabilities and enhance trading liquidity, as well as measures to strengthen equities research coverage.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: Trading volumes in the first quarter of 2026 rose 32% from the previous quarter to $126 billion, and the volumes in March were the highest in almost 20 years.

sections.label: US prospectus disclosure requirements
sections.summary: MAS will make regulations under Part 13A to incorporate applicable US prospectus disclosure requirements for the GLB.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: In the case of the GLB, MAS will make regulations under Part 13A to incorporate the applicable US prospectus disclosure requirements.

sections.label: Aligning Singapore US listing timeline
sections.summary: MAS will align Singapore's listing timeline with the US by varying provisions on the prospectus registration process.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: In the case of the GLB, MAS will align Singapore's listing timeline with that of the US by varying provisions relating to the prospectus registration process.

sections.label: Safe harbours for market misconduct
sections.summary: The Bill enables MAS to set regulations adopting safe harbours as defences to SFA market misconduct provisions.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: The Bill will enable MAS to set regulations to adopt safe harbours as defences to the market misconduct provisions in the SFA.

sections.label: Issuer lodges prospectus for DRs
sections.summary: The Bill clarifies the company issuing underlying shares, not the intermediary financial institution, must lodge its prospectus for DRs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: For avoidance of doubt, the Bill clarifies that it should be the company issuing the underlying shares that is the entity required to lodge its prospectus for registration, instead of the financial institution that acts as an intermediary when issuing the DRs.

sections.label: Dual listing bridge support
sections.summary: The speaker supports the Bill, noting the dual listing bridge targets Asian companies with market capitalisation of $2 billion and above.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: I, therefore, speak in support of the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: It has been announced that the dual listing bridge is targeting companies in Asia with market capitalisation of $2 billion and above to simultaneously access growth capital and liquidity across the US and Asia.

sections.label: Overseas exchange IOSCO safeguard
sections.summary: One safeguard requires the overseas exchange to operate in a jurisdiction whose securities laws are consistent with IOSCO principles.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: One essential safeguard is that the overseas exchange must operate in a jurisdiction whose securities laws are consistent with IOSCO principles.

sections.label: Timeline for dual listing regulations
sections.summary: The passage asks whether there is a timeline for the regulations so the dual listing bridge can be operational.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Is there a timeline by which such regulations will be ready, so that the dual listing bridge can be operational?

sections.label: Issuer responsibility for underlying securities
sections.summary: The Bill places responsibility on the issuer of the underlying securities, aligning legal accountability with economic substance and reducing investor ambiguity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: By placing responsibility on the issuer of the underlying securities, the Bill aligns legal accountability with economic substance and reduces ambiguity for investors.

sections.label: Safeguards, SDRs and review timelines
sections.summary: The passage asks about safeguards and recourse for Singapore investors, whether MAS sees SDRs as transitional or parallel, and about measurable outcomes and review timelines.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Will there be sufficient safeguards to ensure that Singapore investors have clear avenues of recourse in the event of misconduct or disclosure failures?

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: And does MAS see SDRs as a transitional pathway towards fuller listings, or as a parallel structure that could grow in significance over time?

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: The implementation of these recommendations appears to have been phased, with announcements across February, July and November 2025.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Are we seeing measurable outcomes from the earlier initiatives and what review timelines are in place to refine or recalibrate policies?

sections.label: Clearer dual listing arrangements
sections.summary: The Bill aims to create clearer and smoother arrangements for dual listings between the SGX and overseas exchanges.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: First, this Bill aims to create clearer and smoother arrangements for dual listings between the SGX and overseas exchanges.

sections.label: Earlier investor engagement allowed
sections.summary: The Bill lets companies engage investors at an earlier stage of the listing process.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Second, the Bill allows companies to begin engaging investors at an earlier stage of the listing process.

sections.label: Investor engagement and depositary receipts liability
sections.summary: The Bill clarifies depositary receipt liability, placing primary liability on the underlying company rather than the issuing intermediary.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: At the same time, in today's environment where social media spreads information very quickly, we must ensure that "earlier investor engagement" does not become "earlier market sentiment-making." Third, this Bill also clarifies the legal liability relating to depositary receipts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: The Bill makes clear that if there are errors or omissions, the primary liability lies with the underlying company, not with the intermediary that issued the certificate.

sections.label: Safeguards and retail investor participation
sections.summary: Safeguards must remain robust against market volatility and cybersecurity threats, and retail investor participation should be strengthened.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: While we support efficiency and accessibility, safeguards must remain robust to manage new forms of risk, including market volatility and cybersecurity threats.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: We should also take this opportunity to further strengthen retail investor participation in our market.

sections.label: Accountability and integrity standards
sections.summary: Reforms should ensure capital market growth is matched by equally strong accountability and integrity standards.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Any reforms we pursue should reinforce this foundation, ensuring that growth in our capital markets is matched by equally strong standards of accountability and integrity.

sections.label: Three implementation priorities
sections.summary: Implementation must reduce duplication, improve market communication efficiency, and ensure clear responsibilities and investor protection.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: What is most critical is that implementation gets three things right: one, reducing unnecessary duplication in processes; two, improving the efficiency of market communication without compromising fairness and transparency; and three, as we pursue greater international connectivity, ensuring that responsibilities are clear and investors are protected.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: If all three are achieved, I believe this Bill will help Singapore's capital market can achieve long-term steady growth.

sections.label: Singapore and Hong Kong market comparison
sections.summary: The passage compares SGX and Hong Kong Stock Exchange trading values and IPO amounts raised.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: SGX's securities daily average value stands at around $2.4 billion, or US$1.8 billion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Meanwhile, the Hong Kong Stock Exchange records an average daily turnover of HK$304 billion, approximately US$39 billion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: In the first quarter of 2026, Singapore's IPOs raised US$967.1 million.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: In that same period, Hong Kong's secondary listings alone raised US$8.5 billion.

sections.label: Settlement and price stabilisation consultation
sections.summary: Current consultation materials do not prescribe how settlement, closing and price stabilisation will operate across Nasdaq and SGX.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Current consultation materials do not prescribe how settlement, closing and price stabilisation will operate across Nasdaq and SGX.

sections.label: Equity programmes and tracking framework
sections.summary: The S$6.5 billion Equity Market Development Programme and S$1 billion Startup SG Equity top-up are important, and MAS and Enterprise Singapore are asked to identify companies that could reach GLB eligibility in five to seven years and publish a tracking framework.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The S$6.5 billion Equity Market Development Programme and the S$1 billion Startup SG Equity top-up are important initiatives.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: But the path from a start up to a GLB eligible company takes years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: I ask MAS and Enterprise Singapore to identify the cohort of companies that could realistically reach this stage within five to seven years and to publish a framework that allows this House to track progress.

sections.label: Contingency measures for near-IPO companies
sections.summary: MAS is urged to consider contingency measures, including bridging capital through platforms such as ADDX and other flexible funding solutions, so near-IPO companies are not lost due to timing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: A framework without issuers is not a market.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: I urge the MAS to consider contingency measures, including bridging capital through platforms, such as ADDX and other flexible funding solutions, so that near-IPO companies are not lost due to timing.

sections.label: Singapore listed company valuations and sectors
sections.summary: As of May 2026, more than 40 Singapore-listed companies are valued above S$2 billion, mainly in financial services, REITs and some industrials and engineering, with financial services at about 40% capitalisation, real estate 20% and IT 5%.

sentences.speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: As of May 2026, I did a check, there are about more than 40 companies listed in Singapore that are more than S$2 billion in valuation, primarily in financial services, quite a bit of them in Real Estate Investment Trusts and a couple of them in industrials and engineering.

sentences.speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The capitalisation of the financial services in our stock exchanges is about 40%; 20% for real estates; for IT, 5%.

sections.label: Deep-tech listing targets
sections.summary: The Government is asked whether it will target a percentage, in quantity and market cap, for deep-tech companies among new listings to build a technology and innovation hub.

sentences.speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: First, will the Government target a certain percentage, in terms of quantity and market cap, for deep-tech companies as part of our new listing companies' landscape, such as to build up a hub of technology and innovation?

sections.label: Special pathway for deep-tech companies
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether a special pathway would be considered for pre-commercialisation, deep-tech companies, especially in pharma and biotech, given their high potential and scalability.

sentences.speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Do we have the policy to stomach that, losing but very high valuation, because of very high potential, and highly scalable?

sentences.speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: So, when it comes to all these highly scalable companies or tech ventures, would you consider a special pathway for such pre-commercialisation, deep-tech companies, especially in pharma and biotech.

sections.label: Bill dual listings and Sponsored DRs
sections.summary: The Bill has two main elements: legislative changes for dual listings and refinements to improve regulatory oversight, especially Sponsored DRs.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The Bill has two main elements: legislative changes to facilitate dual listings and refinements to improve regulatory oversight, especially concerning Sponsored DRs.

sections.label: Dual listing liquidity concerns
sections.summary: Pushing for dual listing may paradoxically cause scarce local liquidity to leak away into foreign shores.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Our moves to push for dual listing then may paradoxically result in our already scarce local liquidity leaking away into foreign shores.

sections.label: Price discovery and trading volume
sections.summary: Price discovery remains rooted in the US, with average trading volume around 83,000 shares as of April this year.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Price discovery remains firmly rooted in the US and average trading volume, as of April this year, was just around 83,000 shares.

sections.label: Hong Kong cross listings comparison
sections.summary: Cross listings with Hong Kong have underperformed on SGX, in contrast to Stock Connect, which raised HK$78 billion in the first half of 2025.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Cross listings with Hong Kong, the exchange with the largest share of cross listings on the SGX have underperformed here in strict contrast to the Hong Kong exchanges Stock Connect with the Chinese mainland; which raised HK$78 billion Hong Kong in the first half of 2025 alone.

sections.label: Pairing replaces liability provisions
sections.summary: Once a pairing is declared, regulations can replace, modify or disapply core liability provisions, including market misconduct and prospectus liability sections.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: After all, once a pairing is declared, regulations can replace, modify or disapply core liability provisions, including market misconduct in sections 197 to 202 and prospectus liability in sections 253 to 254.

sections.label: MAS foreign law defences
sections.summary: Section 309H permits MAS to substitute defences from foreign jurisdictions' law, so a Singaporean retail investor could face a foreign-rooted defence.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Section 309H permits MAS to substitute defences drawn from the foreign jurisdictions' law.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: A Singaporean retail investor bringing a misrepresentation claim could potentially face a defence rooted in the US Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) rules, or those of another foreign regime, which may presently be unavailable under Singaporean law.

sections.label: Dual listing board transfers
sections.summary: Asks how the dual listing board framework caters to potential transfers given its $2 billion market cap minimum.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Similarly, how does the Government expect the dual listing board framework to cater to potential transfers from either the SGX Main Board or catalyst when its $2 billion market cap minimum appears structurally designed for larger listings than realistically possible for local or regional firms?

sections.label: Member's Commonwealth Capital Group role
sections.summary: Declares that the speaker is Group Managing Director of Commonwealth Capital Group, a Singapore global enterprise.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Loh (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Before I begin, I declare that I am the Group Managing Director of Commonwealth Capital Group, a Singapore global enterprise operating a conglomerate of businesses.

sections.label: Spillovers beyond financial services
sections.summary: States the arrangements do not guarantee spillovers beyond the financial services sector.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Loh (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: First, the arrangements do not guarantee spillovers beyond the financial services sector.

sections.label: Dual listing and mid-sized companies
sections.summary: Says mid-sized local or regional companies are unlikely to benefit, and urges focus on helping high-growth mid-sized companies while keeping listing quality.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Loh (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: They could perhaps be encouraged to dual list in Singapore, with the benefit of some additional liquidity from Asian-focused investors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Loh (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: But mid-sized companies with a more local or regional presence are unlikely to benefit from this arrangement, as they would not typically be considered for listing on global exchanges like the Nasdaq.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Loh (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: And so, we should also continue to focus on helping ambitious, high-growth mid-sized companies to raise the capital they need, so that we can accelerate their growth and create more good jobs for Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Loh (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: That said, we should resist the temptation to lower the quality bar and avoid companies with poor business fundamentals or bad corporate governance to list on the SGX.

sections.label: GLB market capitalisation thresholds
sections.summary: States the consultation set GLB thresholds very high, at around $2 billion in market capitalisation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Shi Xuan (Sembawang)
sentences.text: From the consultation, the thresholds for the GLB are very high, at around $2 billion in market capitalisation.

sections.label: Eligible companies under GLB
sections.summary: Asks MAS whether it can estimate the number of companies potentially eligible under the GLB framework.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Shi Xuan (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Just as my Government Parliamentary Committee Chairman Mr Saktiandi asked, I would also like to check with MAS if they are able to provide an estimated number of companies that are potentially eligible under the GLB framework.

sections.label: Discretion in dual-listing regime
sections.summary: Investors and issuers need clarity on how discretion will be exercised in dual-listing, especially on disclosure recognition and SGX RegCo suspension or delisting.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Shi Xuan (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Whilst discretion is a normal feature of any listing regime, investors and issuers will need clarity on how that discretion will be exercised in the dual-listing context, particularly in relation to disclosure recognition and the circumstances in which SGX RegCo may suspend or delist a company from the GLB.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Shi Xuan (Sembawang)
sentences.text: We need to ensure that this flexibility and discretion do not come at the expense of clarity and investor confidence because Singapore has always competed on clarity, not ambiguity.

sections.label: Singapore capital raising requirement
sections.summary: The framework requires companies to raise $75 million or 15% of the global offering through Singapore, whichever is higher.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The framework requires that companies raise a portion of their capital through Singapore – $75 million or 15% of the global offering, whichever is higher.

sections.label: Singapore's role beyond access
sections.summary: The passage asks what role Singapore can play beyond access and how its market can remain active if trading volumes concentrate in the US.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: If price discovery generally happens in the US due to deeper liquidity, what role can Singapore play beyond access?

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: If trading volumes concentrate in the US, how can we ensure our market also remains active rather than symbolic, given lower trading liquidity?

sections.label: Minimum market capitalisation threshold
sections.summary: The draft listing rules set a minimum $2 billion market capitalisation at listing threshold, among other criteria.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The draft listing rules set out a minimum $2 billion in market capitalisation at listing threshold, among other criteria.

sections.label: Capital raised through Singapore
sections.summary: The passage refers to the requirement that companies raise a meaningful portion of their capital through Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: For example, as I earlier mentioned, the requirement that companies raise a meaningful portion of their capital through Singapore.

sections.label: Concentration of US activity
sections.summary: If trading volumes concentrate in the US, market-making, derivatives, financial intermediation, analyst coverage and valuation influence will also concentrate there.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: If trading volumes concentrate in the US, then market-making activity, derivatives trading and a significant portion of financial intermediation will also concentrate there.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: If analysts' coverage, investor engagement and prospectus requirements are primarily US-led, then much of the influence over valuation and requirements for US capabilities and professional services will sit outside of Singapore.

sections.label: Time zone disclosure requirements
sections.summary: The framework requires ongoing SEC EDGAR disclosures to be announced via SGXNet and other material disclosures released in Singapore within one trading day.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: While the framework recognises time zone differences by requiring ongoing disclosures made on the SEC EDGAR system by the issuer to be announced via SGXNet, at the same time; and other material disclosures made by the issuer will be required to be released in Singapore via SGXNet within one trading day after the date they are filed in the US, timeliness for market's sensitive information is crucial.

sections.label: CEO interest and dual-listed issuers
sections.summary: The speaker declares interest as CEO of an investment management company, saying the Bill offers flexibility for applying the Securities and Futures Act to dual-listed issuers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Victor Lye (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: In doing so, I declare my interest as the CEO of an investment management company.

sentences.speaker: Mr Victor Lye (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: This Bill offers flexibility to calibrate how our Securities and Futures Act applies to dual-listed issuers.

sections.label: Measuring success by liquidity
sections.summary: Success should be measured not only by the number of listings but by whether liquidity is deeply anchored, creating jobs in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Victor Lye (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: We may gain the headline but lose the heartbeat.

sentences.speaker: Mr Victor Lye (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Therefore, success should not be measured only by the number of companies that list here, but whether liquidity – measured by sustainable trading activity, research coverage, investor participation and price discovery are deeply anchored, creating jobs in Singapore.

sections.label: Bottlenecks and growth pipeline
sections.summary: Given the $2 billion minimum market cap threshold, bottlenecks across the capital chain should be identified so the GLB ends a strong Singapore growth pipeline.

sentences.speaker: Mr Victor Lye (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Second, given the $2 billion minimum market cap threshold, can we identify bottlenecks across the capital chain – from startup funding to growth capital before reaching public-markets – so the GLB is not just a listing window, but the end to a strong Singapore pipeline of growth companies.

sections.label: Asian time-zone price discovery node
sections.summary: The amendments to the Securities and Futures Act, including the sponsored depositary receipt framework and the GLB, are forward-looking.

sentences.speaker: Mr Victor Lye (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: If we are merely a Singapore window shadowing another liquid overseas market, we have not succeeded.

sentences.speaker: Mr Victor Lye (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: But if we become an Asian time-zone node for global price discovery, anchored by genuine investor protections, supported by self-sustaining liquidity and part of a broader network connecting capital across regions that can benefit from the Singapore as the capital umbrella – then we will have created something of lasting value.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: The amendments to the Securities and Futures Act, particularly, the introduction of the sponsored depositary receipt framework and the GLB – are forward-looking.

sections.label: MAS and tokenised securities compatibility
sections.summary: The question asks what steps MAS will take to ensure the framework is forward-compatible with tokenised representations of securities and to strengthen liquidity, reduce costs and expand access.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: What steps will MAS take to ensure that this framework is forward-compatible with tokenised representations of securities, and how will we leverage these developments to strengthen liquidity, reduce transaction costs and expand investor access over time?

sections.label: MAS intermediary participation expansion
sections.summary: MAS is asked what steps it will take to expand participation among qualified intermediaries and service providers and support efficient, competitive market activity long term.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: What steps will MAS take to expand participation among qualified intermediaries and service providers and ensure the ecosystem supports efficient and competitive market activity over the long run?

sections.label: MAS success indicators and benchmarks
sections.summary: MAS should track success through trading volume, liquidity, investor participation and capital raised, and the Minister is asked how MAS will define success and benchmarks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: MAS should track success through clear indicators: trading volume, liquidity, investor participation and capital raised through Singapore, not just the number of listings.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: So, I would like to ask the Minister: how will the MAS define success for this framework and what benchmarks will guide its implementation?

sections.label: Two billion dollar listing threshold
sections.summary: The $2 billion threshold reflects SGX and Nasdaq assessments for simultaneous listing success, and GLB issuers must meet a minimum Singapore fundraising requirement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: The choice of the $2 billion threshold reflects what SGX and Nasdaq have assessed to be the conditions for such a simultaneous listing to succeed, so that GLB issuers have sufficient scale and interest from investors in both the US and Singapore markets.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: GLB issuers must also meet a minimum fundraising requirement in Singapore, as this will help to anchor a good level of trading liquidity in Singapore.

sections.label: Funds and market-making measures
sections.summary: The Equity Market Development Programme and Anchor Fund are growing institutional investors, while MAS and SGX will put in place measures to improve market-making.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: Second, specific investment funds in Singapore, such as the $6.5 billion Equity Market Development Programme and the $3 billion Anchor Fund are growing the pool of institutional investors in Singapore who can potentially act as cornerstone investors for Singapore IPOs, including those on the GLB.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: Third, MAS and SGX will be putting in place targeted measures to improve our market-making ecosystem which will facilitate tighter trading spreads and better trading liquidity.

sections.label: Growth Capital Work Group formation
sections.summary: The Growth Capital Work Group was formed in February this year to identify strategies supporting financing solutions for companies before they access public equities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: (In English): "Press forward with speed, without pause or rest, only then can you lead the pack and achieve success." Sir, we are complementing the improvements in our public markets by forming the Growth Capital Work Group in February this year, to identify strategies to support the provision of financing solutions to companies across the various growth stages before they are ready to access the public equities market.

sections.label: GLB expands fund-raising options
sections.summary: The GLB expands the range of fund-raising options Singapore can offer to both domestic and international companies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: The GLB expands the range of fund-raising options that Singapore can offer to both domestic and international companies.

sections.label: MAS regulations for GLB
sections.summary: MAS regulations for the GLB will focus on rules for the GLB, preserving disclosure, governance and enforcement standards, and permitting dual listings only with exchanges in jurisdictions consistent with IOSCO standards.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: The regulations that the MAS will be issuing around middle of this year will focus on the rules that apply to the GLB.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: Members emphasised the need to preserve our standards of disclosure, governance and enforcement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: We will only permit dual listing arrangements with exchanges that operate in an overseas jurisdiction whose securities laws are consistent with IOSCO's international standards and principles.

sections.label: Investor recourse under SFA
sections.summary: Investors in GLB-listed capital market products can use existing SFA recourse options to seek compensation in Singapore Courts for losses from disclosure breaches and market misconduct.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: An investor who invests in capital market products listed on the GLB can utilise the existing investor recourse options that are provided under the SFA to seek compensation for losses arising from breaches of disclosure requirements and market misconduct in the Singapore Courts.

sections.label: MAS consultation on civil compensation
sections.summary: MAS has consulted on proposals to expand investors' ability to obtain civil compensation for losses from market misconduct.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: MAS has consulted on proposals that would expand investors' ability to obtain civil compensation for losses arising from market misconduct.

sections.label: DR issuer disclosure responsibility
sections.summary: The Bill's amendments clarify that the issuer of securities represented by DRs is responsible for compliance with disclosure standards.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: The amendments in this Bill clarify one aspect of this, which is that the issuer of securities that are represented by the DRs will be responsible for compliance with disclosure standards.

sections.label: Technology-neutral regulatory framework
sections.summary: The regulatory framework is technology-neutral, accommodating tokenised and non-tokenised securities based on the principle of same activity, same risk, same regulatory outcome.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: Indeed, our regulatory framework is designed to be technology-neutral and it is able to accommodate both tokenised and non-tokenised securities – the regulatory requirements are premised on the principle of "same activity, same risk, same regulatory outcome".

sections.label: Proposed framework and market momentum
sections.summary: The proposed framework, anchored on international standards and safeguards, aims to enable Singapore to seize opportunities while protecting investors, building on the equities market's positive momentum.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: The proposed framework we have put in place, anchored on strong international standards and with appropriate safeguards in place, is a timely move to enable Singapore to seize new opportunities while ensuring sufficient protection for investors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: The positive momentum we are seeing in our equities market since the Equities Market Review Group submitted our recommendations last November is encouraging, but as I mentioned earlier – never stopping here, this is our ongoing marathon, we will keep going.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: There are some areas for improvement and we will work on these areas to continue to do better.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: This Bill will build on our solid foundation and further raise Singapore's standing as a listing venue of choice and provide a vital bridge with regional and global capital markets.

sections.label: Two billion dollar threshold
sections.summary: The $2 billion threshold may exclude some Main Board companies and means not all companies can join the GLB.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: So, the first part is whether the $2 billion will be too high a threshold, including for some of the companies that are currently on our Main Board and who are looking to list, but may not meet this threshold.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: I accept that the threshold means that not all companies can qualify to come onto the GLB.

sections.label: Two billion dollar level
sections.summary: After discussions, $2 billion was felt to be about the right level.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: After some discussions, we felt that, as I explained in my response speech, $2 billion would be about the right level.

sections.label: Overseas exchange collaborations
sections.summary: SGX will explore working with other exchanges that meet safeguards of high standards and adequate coverage, and the threshold may differ.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: So, certainly, if there are other exchanges that would like to work with SGX, we will be very happy to explore these opportunities and to discuss with them, provided they meet those two important safeguards that I outlined in my speech – high standards, they are able to benefit from adequate coverage; and we will then discuss with the overseas exchange on some of the details.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: We may not end up with a $2 billion threshold because it depends on the size of the other exchange.

sections.label: Case by case judgement
sections.summary: Judgement will be case by case, and more collaborations are welcomed to boost the financial centre's standing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: We will have to judge, case by case.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: But certainly, we look forward to more of such collaborations because that will help to boost our overall standing as a financial centre.
